halloween-grayscale-complete.vo: One hundred pages of Halloween in a single book. Owls on gates, haunted houses, a skeleton on a penny-farthing, two skeletons waltzing beneath a chandelier. The shading is already done, so you just lay your colour over the top. Every page single-sided, nothing bleeds through. Halloween Grayscale, the complete collection. Look inside, link below.

halloween-grayscale-vol1.vo: Fifty pages of autumn, waiting for your colour. Owls, pumpkin patches, apothecary shelves, misty forest paths and haunted houses. These are grayscale designs. The shading is done for you, so every page comes out rich and dimensional with coloured pencils. Halloween Grayscale, volume one. Look inside, link below.

halloween-grayscale-vol2.vo: Fifty little Victorian ghost stories, told in pencil. A skeleton on a penny-farthing. A witch resting in her herb garden. A nursery of antique dolls, a foggy Victorian street. Grayscale shading already in place, so you colour the mood, not the outlines. Halloween Grayscale, volume two. Look inside, link below.

christmas-grayscale-vol1.vo: Fifty pages of midwinter, waiting for your colour. Robins on snowy branches, reindeer in falling snow, log cabins in the pines, a fireside with stockings on the mantel. Grayscale designs, so the shading is done and your pencils do the rest. Christmas Grayscale, volume one. Look inside, link below.

christmas-grayscale-vol2.vo: Santa filling the stockings by the fire. A red fox crossing deep snow. A toymaker at his bench, a stag among the winter birches. Fifty grayscale Christmas scenes with the shading already done, so every page looks finished the moment you add colour. Christmas Grayscale, volume two. Look inside, link below.

christmas-grayscale-complete.vo: One hundred pages of Christmas in a single book. Every design from volumes one and two, quiet pages and busy pages shuffled together. Robins, reindeer, snowy villages, Santa by the fire. The shading is already done, you bring the colour. Christmas Grayscale, the complete collection. Look inside, link below.

into-the-wild.vo: Fifty wild animals, each set in its own botanical world. Foxes, wolves, lions, pandas, sea turtles and eagles, drawn in soft grayscale so the shading is already done. You layer your pencils over the top and the animal comes to life. Into the Wild, a grayscale colouring book for adults. Look inside, link below.

mythic-kingdoms.vo: Open a door into a world of magic. Mighty dragons, delicate fairies, graceful mermaids, soaring phoenixes and floating castles, each framed in an ornate border. Fifty grayscale designs with the shading done for you, so every page turns out gallery-worthy. Mythic Kingdoms. Look inside, link below.

dogs-mystery-mosaics.vo: One pen, six simple marks, and one hundred hidden dogs. No colours to choose and nothing to shade. Every square holds a number, every number is one easy mark, and a dog appears square by square. Retrievers, pugs, corgis, dachshunds and huskies. One Hundred Dogs Mystery Mosaics. Look inside, link below.

dysgraphia-kids.hook: For the child who hates handwriting
dysgraphia-kids.vo: If your child dreads handwriting, this is the book that makes it small and kind. Dark letters to trace, then lighter ones, then start dots, then on their own. The same trace and fade method occupational therapists use. Left-handed friendly, one skill per page, ten relaxed minutes a day. Dysgraphia Handwriting Workbook for Kids, ages six to nine. Look inside, link below.

dysgraphia-teens.hook: Handwriting help that doesn't talk down
dysgraphia-teens.vo: Most handwriting books are built for little kids. This one is for ten to fourteen year olds who are sick of being told their writing is messy. Trace and fade practice sized for an older hand, real words, real sentences, and cursive prep. Nothing babyish about it. Dysgraphia Handwriting Workbook for Teens. Look inside, link below.

left-handed-tracing.hook: Made for lefties from letter one
left-handed-tracing.vo: Almost every tracing book was designed for right-handed children. The example sits on the left, and a left hand covers it the moment the pencil goes down. This one puts a guide letter at both ends of every row. Big letters, ages three to five, dyslexia-friendly type. Left-Handed Letter Tracing for Kids. Look inside, link below.

left-handed-handwriting.hook: The model letter on the RIGHT
left-handed-handwriting.vo: Watch a left-handed child write and you see the problem in seconds. Their hand hides the example they are copying. This workbook puts the model letter on the right, where a left hand can always see it, plus a paper angle and grip guide. Letters, numbers, words and sentences, ages five to ten. Left-Handed Handwriting Workbook for Kids. Look inside, link below.

pre-writing-skills.hook: The book before the handwriting book
pre-writing-skills.vo: Ask a four year old to write an A before they can draw a straight line and you get tears. Handwriting starts with shapes. Straight lines, zig-zags, waves, loops, circles and spirals, with big guides and four slots per row. Then the first easy letters. Pre-Writing Skills Workbook for Little Hands, ages four to six. Look inside, link below.

halloween-word-search-easy.hook: Big letters. Easy words. No tricks.
halloween-word-search-easy.vo: Eighty Halloween word searches with genuinely large print. Words run forwards only, across, down or diagonal, never backwards, so nobody is left stuck. Pumpkin patch, toffee apples, the haunted house, trick or treat. Solutions at the back. Happy Halloween Word Search, easy edition, for adults and seniors. Look inside, link below.

halloween-word-search-hard.hook: All eight directions. Nothing off limits.
halloween-word-search-hard.vo: Same big clear grids, difficulty turned up. Eighty Halloween word searches where words run in all eight directions, forwards, backwards and every diagonal. Big letters, so it is a challenge for your brain and not your eyes. Solutions at the back. Happy Halloween Word Search, hard edition. Look inside, link below.

born-1951.vo: Somebody you love was born in 1951. Give them the year back. One hundred and one short chapters about the world they were born into, eight word searches, forty quiz questions, keepsake pages, all in large print. The birthday present that gets read out loud at the table. One Hundred and One Things People Born in 1951 Will Never Forget. Look inside, link below.

born-1960.vo: Somebody you love was born in 1960. Give them the year back. Eisenhower in the White House, a gallon of petrol for a quarter, the first televised debates. One hundred and one short chapters, eight word searches, forty quiz questions, large print. One Hundred and One Things People Born in 1960 Will Never Forget. Look inside, link below.

born-1966.vo: Somebody you love turns sixty. Give them 1966 back. Batman and Star Trek on the telly, a first-class stamp for five cents, a brand new house for twenty-one thousand dollars. One hundred and one short chapters, eight word searches, forty quiz questions, large print. One Hundred and One Things People Born in 1966 Will Never Forget. Look inside, link below.

puzzles.hook: Puzzles that feel like a cup of tea
puzzles.vo: Most puzzle books are too hard, or too small to read. Gentle Puzzles for Seniors was made differently. Ninety large print puzzles. Word searches that only run across and down, friendly mazes, familiar sayings to finish, and easy number grids. No clock, no score, no wrong way. A kind gift for a parent or grandparent. Look inside, link below.

sea-otter.vo: Forty-four sea otters drawn in thick clean lines with big open spaces. Floating on their backs, holding paws, curled up in kelp. Bold and easy, so it works for kids, beginners and anyone who wants to switch off without fiddly detail. Cute Sea Otter Colouring Book. Look inside, link below.

animal-football.hook: A lion striker. A penguin in goal.
animal-football.vo: A lion striker, a penguin goalkeeper, a crocodile referee with his little red card. Twenty-four football scenes drawn just for small hands, big pictures, thick lines, nothing fiddly. Ages three to eight. Animal Football All-Stars, the bold and easy football colouring book. Look inside, link below.

axolotl.vo: Say hello to the internet's favourite little water friend. Forty-four axolotl scenes in thick, clean, bold outlines. Blowing bubbles, riding a turtle, napping on a rock. No tiny details, no stress, just relax and fill them in. Axolotl Bold and Easy Colouring Book. Look inside, link below.

axolotls-bold-easy.vo: Fifty adorable axolotls with thick outlines and plenty of open space. Tea parties, hot air balloons, pumpkin patches and Christmas stockings. Every design on its own page with a blank back, so markers never bleed through. For kids, teens and grown-ups alike. Adorable Axolotls Bold and Easy. Look inside, link below.

hedgehog.vo: There is something quietly lovely about colouring a little hedgehog at the end of a long day. Fifty of them. Curled in autumn leaves, sipping cocoa, in a cosy scarf, at a tea party under the stars. Thick lines and big open spaces, so it is easy and calm. Hedgehog Bold and Easy. Look inside, link below.

capybara.vo: The world's calmest animal, in the world's calmest colouring book. Fifty capybara scenes in thick, clean lines with big simple shapes. Hot springs, cafes, space helmets and flower crowns. No fiddly details, no stress, just grab your pens. Capybara Bold and Easy. Look inside, link below.

redpanda.vo: Cuter than a cat, and much easier to colour. Fifty red panda scenes in thick, clean, bold outlines. Sipping cocoa, hugging bamboo, flying a kite, baking cookies. Every page backs onto a blank one, so markers are fine. Red Panda Bold and Easy. Look inside, link below.

summer-seek-and-find.vo: Fifty sunny summer scenes, and twelve hidden objects in every one. A busy beach, a funfair, a farm visit, a camping trip. Find them, tick them off, then colour the whole page. Two activities in one for ages four to eight. Summer Seek and Find. Look inside, link below.

halloween-seek-and-find.vo: Fifty friendly Halloween scenes with twelve hidden objects in each. A spooky trick or treat street, a witch's kitchen, a haunted bakery, a bat cave. Gently spooky, never scary. Find them, tick them off, then colour the page. Ages four to eight. Halloween Seek and Find. Look inside, link below.

christmas-seek-and-find.hook: Hidden pictures for the longest wait of the year
christmas-seek-and-find.vo: Fifty Christmas scenes, twelve hidden objects in every one. Santa's workshop, a snowy village, the reindeer stable, a gingerbread kitchen. Search, count, circle and colour. Made for the longest wait of the year, ages four to eight. Christmas Seek and Find. Look inside, link below.

little-star.hook: For small people who fight sleep like heroes
little-star.vo: High in the velvet night sky, all the little stars are falling asleep. All except one. Stella watches the whole world drift off to bed, the rabbits, the ducklings, the old dog by the fire, until the gentle moon shows her how. A soothing bedtime picture book for ages three to eight. The Little Star Who Couldn't Sleep. Look inside, link below.

alien-in-my-shed.vo: One night, a little boy hears the strangest sound. Down in the garden, the old wooden shed is glowing. Inside is Pip, a small green alien with big starry eyes. Three complete bedtime stories in one book, a secret friend, a trip through the planets, and a birthday surprise. Ages three to seven. The Alien I Found in My Shed. Look inside, link below.

goodnight-capybara.hook: The calmest animal on earth, at bedtime
goodnight-capybara.vo: Coco the capybara is not ready for bed. There is still splashing to do, fireflies to chase, and a whole warm river to play in. But as the moon climbs, Mama knows just how to help her wriggliest little one slow down. A cosy rhyming bedtime story for ages two to six. Goodnight, Little Capybara. Look inside, link below.

jackdaw.vo: Some children's books are painted, not produced. Every spring the jackdaws come back to the old cottage garden. This year one young jackdaw tumbles from the flock with a broken wing, and a kind hedgehog finds him. A gentle story about patience, kindness and learning to fly again. Ages five to nine. The Jackdaw with a Broken Wing. Look inside, link below.

mole-worms.vo: Like all moles, Mike lives underground and eats worms. There is just one problem. Mike really, really does not like them. With a robin called Ralph and a rabbit called Ronald, he sets off to discover what a mole who won't eat worms could possibly eat instead. A funny, gentle read-aloud with soft watercolour art, ages five to nine. The Mole Who Wouldn't Eat Worms. Look inside, link below.

lonely-badger.hook: For quiet kids with big hearts
lonely-badger.vo: Deep in the quiet countryside, a shy young badger named Brian lives all alone. Then one moonlit evening he hears soft crying from a bramble bush, and everything changes. A gentle, beautifully painted story about loneliness, courage and friendship, for ages five to nine. The Lonely Badger. Look inside, link below.

barnaby-hospital.vo: Meet Barnaby, a big friendly blue double-decker bus. One afternoon a lady trips at the zebra crossing and hurts her knee, and Barnaby has a very important job. Carry her safely to the hospital. Big bold pictures that make doctors and hospitals nothing to be scared of, ages three to six. Barnaby Goes to Hospital. Look inside, link below.

dementia.vo: They told you it was dementia, then sent you home with no idea what to do next. This is the calm, practical guide for that moment. What to do in the first week, how to talk to them, the legal and money basics, and how to look after yourself too. Short enough to read in an afternoon. The First Ninety Days of Dementia Care. Look inside, link below.

adhd-5-minute-reset.vo: You buy a planner, miss three days, and the empty pages feel like proof you failed. This one was built for ADHD brains. Undated, so a missed week costs nothing. Brain-dump pages, padded daily plans, twenty-five minute focus sprints and habit trackers that let you restart. No guilt, no streaks. The Five Minute Reset. Look inside, link below.

gross-book-of-why.hook: Why do we fart? Real answers.
gross-book-of-why.vo: Why do we fart? Why is snot green? Why do dogs sniff each other's bottoms? Kids ask, and this book actually answers. One hundred and fifty gross questions with real answers, checked against real science, a drawing for every one, and a quiz in every section. Ages six to twelve. The Curious Kid's Gross Book of Why. Look inside, link below.
